summary: Cas Russell, just released from a station, phones Checker, a hacker-type who forged paperwork and erased her fingerprints from the system so she could be freed. Checker waives payment, saying he owes her for saving Arthur and is grateful she kept Arthur alive. Cas feels uneasy about owing favors and about her conscience, which has taken on the persona of Tresting. When Cas criticizes Arthur as inconsistent, Checker sharply defends him, and the call ends on a tense note.
one_line: Cas Russell, freed from custody with Checker's forged paperwork, phones him and clashes with him over Arthur.
key_facts: Cas Russell phones Checker shortly after she reaches the sidewalk at night, following her release.
Checker says he forged a large amount of paperwork and calls the job record-breaking.
Checker says Cas has nothing in the system, which gave him a window to work with.
Checker says Cas's fingerprints are disappearing from the system as they speak.
Checker waives his fee, saying he owed Cas for saving Arthur and is grateful she kept Arthur alive.
Cas says she does not like owing people favors.
Checker asks Cas not to tell Arthur about the free help because Arthur does not like it when he does such things.
A copy of Tresting has taken up residence in Cas's head and keeps track of her actions.
Cas describes Arthur as inconsistent, saying he breaks many laws yet gets hung up on small things.
Checker sharply responds, 'Hey, he's good people,' and asks Cas not to insult Arthur.
Checker's tone becomes unreadable and he goes silent, leaving Cas uncertain how the call stands.
The night scene describes a nearly full moon above a busy city and red tail lights of cars.
